title: Environmental Monitoring
description: Standard operating procedure for continuous environmental monitoring in aquaculture systems. Covers monitoring system setup, alarm thresholds and responses, data logging procedures, and trend analysis for proactive system management. Early detection of environmental changes prevents organism stress and mortality.

steps.title: Understanding Environmental Monitoring
steps.description: Continuous environmental monitoring provides real-time data on critical parameters affecting organism health. Unlike spot testing, continuous monitoring captures trends, detects sudden changes, and enables rapid response to dangerous conditions. A well-designed monitoring system is the first line of defense against environmental emergencies.

steps.title: Key Parameters for Continuous Monitoring
steps.description: Priority parameters for continuous monitoring include: Temperature (affects metabolism, DO, toxicity), Dissolved Oxygen (immediate life support), pH (affects toxicity and osmoregulation), Salinity/Conductivity (osmotic stress), and Flow Rate (life support function). Additional parameters may include ORP, turbidity, and specific ion concentrations depending on species and system design.

steps.title: Monitoring Station Setup
steps.description: Position monitoring sensors at representative locations in each system. Sensors should be placed where water is well-mixed and represents true system conditions. Avoid dead zones, direct sunlight on sensors, and areas with high debris. Secure sensors to prevent movement and damage.

steps.title: Sensor Installation Checklist
steps.description: Follow checklist when installing or relocating monitoring sensors.
checklistItems: Location represents system conditions (good water flow)

steps.title: Sensor Calibration
steps.description: All sensors require regular calibration to maintain accuracy. Calibration frequency varies by sensor type and manufacturer specifications. Temperature sensors are generally stable; DO and pH sensors require more frequent calibration. Always use fresh, unexpired calibration solutions and follow manufacturer procedures.

steps.title: Calibration Schedule and Documentation
steps.description: Maintain calibration schedule for all monitoring sensors.
checklistItems: Temperature probes: Verify quarterly against reference
pH sensors: Calibrate with 2-point calibration weekly
DO sensors: Calibrate in air-saturated water weekly
Note sensor response time and stability
Update calibration log in monitoring system

steps.title: Alarm Threshold Configuration
steps.description: Alarms must be configured to alert staff before conditions become lethal. Set warning alarms at the edge of optimal range and critical alarms before dangerous thresholds. Alarms that trigger too frequently will be ignored; alarms set too conservatively may not provide adequate warning.
checklistItems: Warning alarms set at edge of optimal range
Critical alarms set before lethal thresholds

steps.title: Recommended Alarm Thresholds
steps.description: General marine aquaculture alarm thresholds (adjust for species): Temperature Warning: plus/minus 2C from target, Critical: plus/minus 4C. DO Warning: <6 mg/L, Critical: <4 mg/L. pH Warning: <7.6 or >8.5, Critical: <7.2 or >8.8. Salinity Warning: plus/minus 3 ppt from target. Flow Warning: <80% of normal, Critical: <50% or zero flow. Always consult species-specific requirements.

steps.title: Alarm Response Protocol
steps.description: When an alarm activates, respond immediately. Acknowledge the alarm to confirm you are responding. Assess the situation quickly. Determine if the alarm is real or a sensor malfunction. Implement corrective action for real alarms. Document all alarm events and responses.

steps.title: Alarm Response Checklist
steps.description: Follow this checklist when responding to any environmental alarm.
checklistItems: If real alarm: Initiate corrective action
If sensor malfunction: Troubleshoot or replace sensor
Monitor until parameter returns to normal

steps.title: Low Dissolved Oxygen Emergency Response
steps.description: Low DO is immediately life-threatening. Response must be rapid. Increase aeration immediately with all available means. Check for pump or blower failure. Add emergency oxygen if available. Reduce feeding. Consider emergency water exchange. Monitor organisms for distress and mortality.
checklistItems: Check air pumps and blowers for failure
Investigate root cause after crisis resolved

steps.title: Temperature Excursion Response
steps.description: Temperature changes affect all biological processes and can be rapidly lethal. For rising temperatures: Increase shade or cooling. Increase water flow. Add chilled water carefully. For falling temperatures: Activate heaters. Reduce water exchange. Add warm water carefully. Never change temperature more than 1-2C per hour to avoid thermal shock.
checklistItems: For high temp: Activate cooling, increase shade/flow
For low temp: Activate heating, reduce exchange
Do not exceed 1-2C change per hour

steps.title: Data Logging and Storage
steps.description: All monitoring data should be logged automatically and stored securely. Data logging intervals depend on the parameter and system dynamics. Typical intervals range from 1-minute for critical alarms to 15-minute for routine logging. Ensure adequate storage capacity and regular data backups.
checklistItems: Logging intervals appropriate for each parameter
Data storage sufficient for required retention
Data accessible for analysis and reporting
Historical data archived according to policy

steps.title: Daily Monitoring System Check
steps.description: Verify monitoring system operation daily. Confirm all sensors are reporting. Check for sensor drift by comparing to portable meters. Review overnight data for anomalies. Clear any pending alarms and investigate causes. Ensure alarm notification is functioning.

steps.title: Daily Monitoring System Verification
steps.description: Complete daily verification of monitoring system function.
checklistItems: Current readings match portable meter spot checks

steps.title: Trend Analysis
steps.description: Regular trend analysis identifies gradual changes before they become emergencies. Review historical data weekly and monthly. Look for gradual drift in baseline values, increasing variability, seasonal patterns, and correlations between parameters. Trend analysis enables proactive management decisions.

steps.title: Weekly Trend Review
steps.description: Review monitoring trends weekly to identify developing issues.
checklistItems: Graph key parameters over past week
Compare to previous weeks and baseline
Identify any gradual drift or changes

steps.title: Sensor Maintenance
steps.description: Sensors require regular maintenance to ensure accuracy. Clean sensors according to manufacturer schedule, typically weekly for optical sensors. Replace consumables (electrolyte, membranes) as specified. Protect sensors from biofouling. Replace sensors at end of service life.
checklistItems: Check membrane condition on electrochemical sensors
Replace sensors at end of service life

steps.title: Monitoring System Redundancy
steps.description: Critical systems should have redundant monitoring. Primary sensor failure should not leave systems unmonitored. Options include duplicate sensors, portable backup meters, and manual monitoring schedules. Test backup monitoring regularly. Know how to operate in degraded mode if primary system fails.

steps.title: Monitoring Documentation
steps.description: Maintain complete documentation of monitoring system configuration and performance.
checklistItems: Contact information for technical support current
